newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's HPI, Marzotto plan merger.
newsitem.headline: Italy's HPI, Marzotto plan merger.

text.p: Newly-formed Italian company Holding di Partecipazioni (HPI) and textiles group Marzotto said they planned to merge into a new firm to be called Gruppo Industriale Marzotto.

In a joint statement, HPI, which was recently spun off from financial holding Gemina, and Marzotto said they planned a share swap ratio of 13 ordinary HPI shares with a nominal value of 500 lire for one ordinary Marzotto share with a nominal value of 1,000 lire.
They also planned to offer eight non-convertible HPI savings shares for one non-convertible Marzotto savings share.
"The proposed operation will create one of the largest groups worldwide in the textiles and clothing sector with a significant position in the editorial (publishing) sector," HPI and Marzotto said.

Based on preliminary 1996 results from both companies, "the new group would have had a turnover and net aggregate result of 8.24 trillion lire and 253 billion lire respectively," the statement said, adding total staff would be more than 21,000.
They said Pietro Marzotto had been proposed as chairman of the new company, Gruppo Industriale Marzotto, while Maurizio Romiti had been nominated managing director.
Current HPI chairman Nicolo Nefri would remain in his post until the merger and would then be proposed as a board member.
